شَتِيتٌ : see شَتٌّ, in four places. ثَغْرٌ شَتِيتٌ means [Fore teeth] separate, or wide-apart, one from another. (S, A, K.) Tarafeh says, “مِنْ شَتِيتٍ كَأَقَاحِ الرَّمْلِ غُرْ
” [meaning From separate fore teeth like white chamomiles of the sands: ثَغْرٍ being understood, and غُرْ being for غُرٍّ]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
